newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Amersham bouyed by Pharmacia link.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Amersham bouyed by Pharmacia link.

text.p: British health and technology group Amersham International Plc ended months of speculation on Tuesday by announcing plans to merge its drug discovery arm with Sweden's Pharmacia Biotech.
The joint venture will create the world's biggest supplier of specialised drug discovery technology, with annual sales of around 430 million pounds ($703.1 million) and more than 3000 employees.
Amersham shares set record highs as analysts applauded the move, which Amersham expects to generate annual cost savings of 30 million pounds by 1999.

By late morning shares in the group, which was the first privatisation of the Thatcher era in Britain, were up 116 1/2 pence at 1467 1/2, after peaking at 15 pounds a share. In Stockholm shares in the Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn also responded positively, though less dramatically, gaining 2 1/2 Swedish crowns to 271 1/2.

Sentiment towards Amersham was further helped by a strong set of results, which saw profits jump by 30 percent in the year to March to 65.8 million pounds on the back of soaring sales for its Myoview heart-imaging agent and a new treatment for prostate cancer.

Amersham told Reuters the two companies had been talking since the start of the year. It was forced to admit its interest in merging Amersham Life Science with Pharmacia Biotech on May 30 after its officials were spotted in Sweden.

"The new company will secure our goal of being the world's leading research-based life science and biotechnology supply company, mirroring the global leadership we have won in nuclear medicine," Amersham chief executive Bill Castell said.

Amersham will own 55 percent of the venture, Amersham Pharmacia Biotech, with P&U holding the remainder. Although Uppsala-based Pharmacia Biotech has higher sales, Amersham Life Science is far more profitable, with profit margins of around 24 percent of sales compared to around nine percent for the Swedish side.

The parent companies have agreed to prepare the joint venture for possible partial flotation on the stock market after January 2000. In addition, P&U will be able to sell its stake to Amersham from 2000 onwards at 10 percent below the then market price, and Amersham has the right to force P&U to sell its holding from 2004.
Castell told Reuters that by 2004 it was likely the unit would have been floated or that Amersham would have taken full ownership.

Cost-cutting will be a major attraction of the joint venture, with around 360 jobs to go over the next two years. The new company will be based in Sweden but will have offices at Amersham in England and Cardiff in Wales.

Pharmacia Biotech's core strengths in instrumentation and software will be supplemented by Amersham's growing prowess in labelling genes and cells and identifying their action in the body, an increasingly important area in the discovery of new drugs.
Analysts said the merger was a personal achievement for Amersham's Castell, who has built up the company's skills in drug discovery systems since taking control in 1990.

It will also leave Amersham's management free to concentrate on its most profitable business, the healthcare arm which creates radioactive treatments and diagnostic tests for conditions including cancer, strokes and Parkinson's disease.
